name: Critical minerals
value: China export-control pauses run to Jan 2027
summary: China keeps rare-earth and gallium export-control suspensions in place under the US trade truce; licensing stays
state: China on 9 Nov extended its suspension of October 2025 export-control measures, including some rare-earth and battery-material curbs, to January 2027, while earlier rare-earth licensing stays in force (S&P Global). Its suspension of a ban on gallium, germanium and antimony exports to the US also remains under the trade truce (Fastmarkets), with Rare Earth Exchanges flagging 27 Nov as a deadline for Western buyers. No production stoppages outside China linked to export bans were found as of 26 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: Makers of magnets, chips and batteries outside China remain exposed to licensing delays and possible renewed curbs.
rubric_hit: Export licensing in force and controls only suspended = Watch; no stoppages outside China

sources.title: S&P Global — China extends rare earth export suspension to January 2027
Fastmarkets — China suspends export prohibition on gallium, germanium, antimony to US
Rare Earth Exchanges — China gallium and germanium controls put Western buyers on a 27 November clock

why: Rare earths, gallium, germanium and graphite are chokepoints for chips, EVs and defence — and China dominates processing.
drivers: Export controls, trade disputes, mine outages, stockpiling.

rubric.alert: Export bans in force that are causing reported production stoppages outside China.
rubric.watch: New export controls announced or licensing slowed.
rubric.normal: No new export restrictions in the past month.
